issues.body:
Unchanged from rounds 3 and 4, and now reproduced by execution. `total` is reduced modulo FIELD_P (2_147_483_647) at every reduce step (mpc-sim.ts:41) and compared directly: `verdict: total >= threshold` (:42). Modular reconstruction is faithful to the real sum only when that sum is < FIELD_P, and nothing enforces that.

Executed counterexample: two parties with value 1_100_000_000 each, threshold 2_000_000_000. True sum 2_200_000_000 >= threshold, so the honest verdict is true. The function returns a reconstructed total of 52_516_353 and verdict === false. Confirmed by running the code, not by inspection. The revealed bit -- the only thing this tool exists to reveal -- is wrong, with no error and no warning.

Inputs are unbounded on both paths: mpc-tool.tsx feeds `Number(event.target.value)` from free-form number inputs (min=0 is not enforced on paste and caps nothing at the top end), and workspaceIntegers() (:46-:54) admits anything passing Number.isSafeInteger (up to 2^53-1), up to 8 of which loadWorkspaceValues() pushes into `values`. An individual party value >= FIELD_P is also silently misrepresented by `mod(value - sum)` at :35 before any summing.
issues.fix_hint: Validate against the field: reject (or clamp with a visible error) any party value < 0 or >= FIELD_P, and assert the plaintext sum < FIELD_P before returning a verdict, surfacing an explicit 'inputs exceed the simulation field' error otherwise. Alternatively compute the verdict from the plaintext sum, or widen to BigInt with a larger modulus. Add a regression test pinning the 1_100_000_000 x2 / threshold 2_000_000_000 counterexample above.
issues.title: Threshold verdict computed on the mod-p total, so any true sum >= FIELD_P silently returns the wrong answer

issues.body:
Unchanged from rounds 3 and 4, and now demonstrated by mutation rather than asserted. The first test makes three assertions: verdict === true, shares.length === 2, localSums.length === 2. The two length assertions are structural only.

I ran a deliberately broken implementation emitting `row = [0, value]` -- no randomness, no field arithmetic, nothing secret-shared -- and it satisfies all three assertions and passes green. The additive-sharing construction, the entire point of the module, has zero behavioural coverage.

Further gaps:
- The below-threshold branch is never exercised: flipping `>=` to `<` at mpc-sim.ts:42 flips only this one case and no test asserts verdict === false.
- The `parties.length < 2` throw (mpc-sim.ts:26) has no test.
- localSums is asserted only by length, and is never read by mpc-tool.tsx (which renders only result.shares and result.verdict), so it is dead output with no behavioural coverage anywhere.
- The injected `random` seam is passed (`() => 0.25`) but no assertion depends on the resulting share values, so the determinism the seam exists to provide is unused.

The workspaceIntegers test is genuine -- it pins dedup and ordering.
issues.fix_hint: Assert the invariants: (1) each share row sums to that party's value mod FIELD_P; (2) sum of localSums mod FIELD_P equals the plaintext total; (3) a below-threshold case asserting verdict === false; (4) assert.throws for a single-party input; (5) with the fixed random seam, pin the concrete expected share matrix. Then confirm the suite goes RED when `>=` is flipped to `<` and when the sharing is replaced by [0, value] -- both currently stay green.
issues.title: Vacuous test: a broken sharing implementation passes green (verified by mutation)

issues.body:
Unchanged from rounds 3 and 4. The four field encodings (ages 24/25/30/42) at zk-prover.ts:4-9 are byte-identical copies of AGE_OPERAND_ENC in site/src/lib/zk-prover.ts, which carries an explicit DRIFT GUARD note (sq-1s2.4) pinning them against the native encoder via crates/sparq-zk-compose/tests/site_age_enc_drift.rs.

Re-verified this round that the guard is site-path-only: it resolves '../../site/src/lib/zk-prover.ts' (site_age_enc_drift.rs:123 and :183) and parses the identifier AGE_OPERAND_ENC (:54-:55). A repo-wide grep for 'gui/app/src/lib/zk-prover' returns NO hits in any .rs, .mjs, .ts or .yml file -- the GUI copy is referenced by no guard and no CI lane. It differs on BOTH axes (different path, different symbol name OPERAND_ENCODING), so even a path-widening fix would not match the renamed identifier.

Consequence: on a circuit/encoder bump the drift test goes red, someone regenerates the site constant per the test's own remediation message, and the GUI copy silently goes stale. GUI proving then fails at witness-solve time -- exactly the failure the site comment warns about. There is no test on the GUI copy and no cross-reference comment pointing back at the guard.

Related (same theme): the provable-age set is duplicated a third time as a hard-coded literal inside zk-tool.tsx, at both the workspaceAges filter (:31) and the select options (:80), rather than consuming the exported PROVABLE_AGES.
issues.fix_hint: Preferred: do not duplicate. Hoist the map into one shared module both site/ and gui/app/ import, leaving exactly one guarded definition. If duplication must stay: (a) keep the identifier AGE_OPERAND_ENC so the existing parser matches, (b) extend site_age_enc_drift.rs to iterate over BOTH paths, asserting each parses non-empty and matches native_enc, and (c) carry the DRIFT GUARD comment into the GUI copy with a pointer to the test. Also have zk-tool.tsx consume PROVABLE_AGES instead of re-listing the ages.
issues.title: Committed operand_enc constants duplicated outside the native drift guard (renamed OPERAND_ENCODING)

issues.body:
Unchanged from rounds 3 and 4. proveAge() performs the full cold start inline on each invocation: the Promise.all dynamic imports plus circuit fetch (:51-:58), then `await bb.Barretenberg.new({ threads: 1 })` (:59) and `new bb.UltraHonkBackend(...)` (:60).

The source it was extracted from deliberately does not: site/src/lib/zk-prover.ts memoises everything behind a single shared proverPromise (:195, loadProver at :231-:254), documents Barretenberg.new as 'the dominant cold cost' (:180), exposes prewarmProver() (:266) so the route pays it off-click, and resets the promise on failure to allow retry (:250-:251). None of that survived -- re-confirmed by grep against the head tree this round.

Two consequences:
- Every click re-pays the dominant cold start (WASM instantiate) plus a redundant circuit re-fetch, so every proof after the first is needlessly slow. The panel has no pre-warm, so the first click pays it on the interaction path.
- Nothing releases the previous Barretenberg instance. Each proof allocates a fresh WASM instance (and its memory) that is dropped on the floor, so repeated proving in a long-lived workbench tab accumulates them. The workbench is a persistent-tab app, unlike the site's one-shot demo page.

The per-call fetch also has no cached-failure reset semantics.
issues.fix_hint: Port loadProver()'s shared-promise pattern: a module-level proverPromise caching { Noir, backend, circuit }, reused across calls and reset to null in a .catch so a transient fetch/instantiate failure retries. Optionally export a prewarm() the ZkTool calls in a mount effect. If a per-call backend is genuinely wanted, release the instance in a finally block instead of leaking it. Simplest and best: import the shared implementation rather than re-deriving it.
issues.title: Prover context rebuilt on every proof: new Barretenberg WASM instance per click, never released

issues.body:
Unchanged from rounds 3 and 4. The done-state block renders the icon unconditionally, outside the ternary:

  <CheckCircle2 className="size-4 text-[var(--success)]" aria-hidden />
  Verification: {state.verified ? "accepted" : "rejected"}

So when verified === false the panel shows a green success checkmark immediately adjacent to the word 'rejected'. The container styling is identical between the two cases. The AlertTriangle/destructive treatment is reserved for the `error` state (a thrown exception) and is never reached by a proof that verifies false.

On a ZK surface this fails in the wrong direction. A failed cryptographic verification is the one outcome the panel must not dress as success -- a user glancing at the green check reasonably reads it as 'the proof checked out'. This panel is what the sq-ixc3.17 tier flip promotes to built: true / tier: live-bbjs (zk-tool.meta.ts), so it is the honesty-bearing surface.

Minor related point in the same block: state.eligible renders as a raw String(boolean) under the label 'Disclosed predicate', which is honest but terse given verified and eligible are independent bits users are likely to conflate.
issues.fix_hint: Branch the icon, colour and container on state.verified: CheckCircle2 with var(--success) only when verified === true; AlertTriangle with the destructive treatment when verified === false. Consider treating verified === false as a distinct prominent state rather than a field inside the success card, since with a correct circuit it should be unreachable and therefore signals something is wrong.
issues.title: A REJECTED verification renders a green success check icon

issues.body:
Unchanged from rounds 3 and 4. Two claims are stronger than the code behind them.

1. The badge reads 'Simulation · honest-majority semi-honest' (:43). That names a specific cryptographic adversary model, but simulateThreshold runs entirely inside one browser tab in one process: there are no parties, no channels, no adversary, and therefore no threat model to be honest-majority or semi-honest with respect to. Attaching the label to an in-memory illustration invites the reader to transfer the native sparq-mpc protocol's (already semi-honest-only) posture onto something that has none. This is squarely in the privacy-claims gate's scope.

2. The header (:40) says the tool will 'Secret-share integer inputs and reveal only whether their sum meets a threshold.' The implementation does not: mpc-sim.ts:41 reconstructs the full plaintext total and the UI then merely chooses to display only the boolean. A real threshold protocol never materialises the sum. 'reveal only X' is a privacy claim, and here the sum is computed in the clear and simply not printed.

Credit where due: the prose paragraph below the header is genuinely good and does most of the honesty work ('in-tab additive-sharing illustration, not the native sparq-mpc protocol and not live networked MPC'), and tier live-sim is the correct taxonomy value. The fix is to bring badge and header in line with that paragraph.
issues.fix_hint: Drop the adversary-model wording from the badge -- 'Simulation · illustrative only' or 'Simulation · no security model' is accurate. Reword the header to what actually happens, e.g. 'Additively secret-share integer inputs and reconstruct their sum to evaluate a public threshold', so no 'reveal only' claim is made. If the reveal-only-the-bit property is wanted for real, the comparison must be performed without reconstructing the total.
issues.title: Badge asserts a specific adversary model, and the header claim overstates what the simulation withholds

issues.body:
Unchanged from rounds 3 and 4. Both new panels do this (zk-tool.tsx workspaceAges :30-:33, and the identical pattern in mpc-tool.tsx workspaceValues :22-:25):

  React.useMemo(() => workspaceIntegers(snapshotStore() ?? ""), [snapshotStore, storeSize])

(a) Wrong invalidation key. engine-context.tsx exposes storeEpoch as the content-change signal (:461) and bumps it whenever the base store content changes (:784-:785, :1188-:1189, :1358-:1359). storeSize is a quad COUNT (:676). Any mutation preserving the count -- a replace, a clear-then-reload of equal size, an edit swapping a literal's value -- leaves the memo stale, so the panel shows integers no longer in the store. Existing callers use storeEpoch for exactly this reason (streaming-tool.tsx:188, forms-tool.tsx:97), re-confirmed by grep this round.

(b) Render-path cost. snapshotStore() serializes the ENTIRE dataset to N-Quads and this runs synchronously during render, then regex-scans the whole string. Every other caller does it inside an effect or a user-triggered callback, never on the render path. On a large store, merely opening the ZK tab blocks the UI to build a hint sentence the user did not ask for -- and in zk-tool the entire result feeds one advisory line.
issues.fix_hint: Swap storeSize for storeEpoch in both dependency arrays. Move the serialization off the render path into a useEffect + useState (matching streaming-tool.tsx), or compute it lazily behind the existing 'Use live workspace integers' button rather than eagerly on mount.
issues.title: Whole-store N-Quads serialization runs synchronously in useMemo, keyed on the wrong change signal

issues.body:
Unchanged from rounds 3 and 4. The extraction inlines `const options = { verifierTarget: "evm" as const }` (:72) with no explanation. The source wraps the same value in a warning that is load-bearing for the ZK property (site/src/lib/zk-prover.ts, PROOF_OPTIONS):

  - ':125 -- We NEVER pass any *-no-zk flavour: those set disableZk:true and strip the ZK masking, which would make the private age recoverable in principle.'
  - ':161-:164 -- @aztec/bb.js is pinned to a NIGHTLY. The verifierTarget option surface can shift between nightlies -- RE-TEST this flavour on ANY bb.js version bump before trusting it. Never substitute a *-no-zk flavour.'

The GUI copy carries neither, while gui/app/package.json now pins the same nightly (@aztec/bb.js 5.0.0-nightly.20260324) as a GUI runtime dependency -- so the nightly caveat applies in a second place with the warning present in only one. A maintainer editing this file has no signal that the flavour string is security-relevant rather than cosmetic.

Also: this module has no unit test and was not added to test:unit (only mpc-sim.test.ts was). The cheaply-testable pure parts -- the operand lookup and its throw (:47-:48), and the padStart/charCodeAt digit encoding (:62) -- are uncovered, despite that digit encoding being exactly the off-by-one class that silently produces an unsatisfiable witness.
issues.fix_hint: Carry the PROOF_OPTIONS comment block (or a one-line pointer to it) into the GUI copy. Add a small zk-prover.test.ts covering: proveAge throws for an age with no committed encoding; the digit encoding for each of the four provable ages matches the expected ASCII pair; AGE_THRESHOLD/PROVABLE_AGES agree. Register it in test:unit alongside mpc-sim.test.ts. Unnecessary if the shared-module consolidation above is done instead.
issues.title: verifierTarget flavour copied without its safety note; bb.js pinned to a nightly with no re-test guard, and no unit test for this module

verdict.summary:
Round 5 of PR #5318 (ZK + MPC workbench tools promoted from stubs to live panels). No commit has landed since round 4: HEAD is still 9a21ceb0, the same tree round 4 reviewed. All eight prior findings reproduce verbatim at the same severities -- stagnant.

Rather than restate the prior round, I re-verified the two load-bearing claims by EXECUTING the code:

1. The mod-p verdict bug is real and reproducible. simulateThreshold with two parties of 1_100_000_000 and threshold 2_000_000_000: true sum 2_200_000_000 clears the threshold, but the reconstructed total comes back 52_516_353 and it returns verdict === false. The one bit this tool exists to reveal is silently wrong, no error. Inputs are unbounded on both paths.

2. The test is genuinely vacuous. I ran a broken implementation emitting row = [0, value] -- no randomness, no field arithmetic, nothing secret-shared -- and it satisfies all three assertions and passes green. The below-threshold branch is never exercised, so flipping >= to < at mpc-sim.ts:42 is not caught; the <2-parties throw is untested; the random seam is injected but unasserted.

Also re-confirmed in the head tree:
- site_age_enc_drift.rs resolves '../../site/src/lib/zk-prover.ts' (:123, :183) and parses AGE_OPERAND_ENC (:54). A repo-wide grep finds NO reference to gui/app/src/lib/zk-prover in any guard or CI lane, and the GUI copy renamed the symbol to OPERAND_ENCODING -- outside the guard on both axes.
- site/src/lib/zk-prover.ts memoises behind proverPromise (:195, :231-:254), calls Barretenberg.new the dominant cold cost (:180), exposes prewarmProver (:266), resets on failure (:250). None survived into the GUI copy.
- engine-context.tsx exposes storeEpoch as the content-change signal (:461); existing callers key on it (streaming-tool.tsx:188, forms-tool.tsx:97). Both new panels key on storeSize, a quad count.
- zk-tool.tsx renders CheckCircle2 unconditionally above 'Verification: rejected'.

Blocking set unchanged.
